decisions.reason: Confirmed: the unbiased estimator taking -p and 3p equally has mean p, variance 4p^2 and bounded RE=2, but is negative with probability 1/2. Restricting only the comparison to nonnegative unbiased families preserves both definitions. For BRE<=C, E[hat p^2]=p^2(1+RE^2), so the logarithmic ratio is 1+log(1+RE^2)/log(p^2), which tends to 1. The work criteria and event-conditioned benchmark remain unchanged.

Confirmed: the library natural-number convention includes 0, so c_s/k^s does not define a mass function on the original Omega=N. Set Omega={1,2,...}, matching the existing sums and contract. Now both masses normalize, Q(k)>0 on the entire domain, Z=(c_2/c_3)k 1_{k>=m} is nonnegative and integrable, E_Q Z=c_2 sum_{k>=m} k^-2=P(A_m)>0, while E_Q Z^2=(c_2^2/c_3) sum_{k>=m} 1/k diverges. The changed efficiency comparison has no effect on F4 or this computation.

Thus A1 and axiom_use accurately describe inherited model assumptions, while the concrete finite construction is choice-free. Confirmed nonfatal nomenclature defect: the supplied SIR algorithm fixes G0=1, so the zero branch concerns first event potential G1=1_A1, not the initial potential. The example already proves the intended positive-probability zero-estimate phenomenon; name G1 correctly and explicitly check the intervening resampling and identity M1. Both initial particles equal 1 with probability 1/4, and all their descendants still miss A1, forcing the first event-weight average and estimate to zero although P(A1)=1/2. This 1/4 event is sufficient and is not asserted to exhaust zero-output runs; enumerating initial particles and ancestor draws gives total zero-output probability 3/8. The proof uses unbiasedness only to explain compatibility, never to infer pathwise positivity.
